title: From Noise to Control: Parameterized Diffusion Policies
claim: Evaluations usually vary inputs, but real failures come from constraint-induced behavior shifts, where steering through noise is unstable and a structured latent is smooth.
layout: 3 stacked rows, left-to-right arrows, bottom row compares two latent spaces
description: The figure has three rows, all built around a humanoid robot kicking a soccer ball at a goal. Top row, 'Observation Adaptation': two training scenes with red and orange floors, then an arrow to a test scene with a brown floor. The same green trajectory appears in every scene. Middle row, 'Behavior Adaptation': the training scene shows four colored trajectory arcs toward an open goal. The test scene adds goalkeepers that block most of the arcs, shown dotted, and a new red trajectory is the one that works. A horizontal divider separates these from the bottom row. Bottom row: on the left, DP's noise space is two nested blue ellipses with a red star (desired latent) and a purple cross (reached latent). On the right, PDP's embedding space is a colorful wavy 3D surface with the same two markers. Both connect to the central goalkeeper scene by solid 'latent inversion' arrows and dotted 'denoising rollout' arrows. Math labels read Δε ∝̸ Δτ (left) and Δz ∝ Δτ (right). A legend runs along the bottom.
caption: Observation-side shift vs. constraint-induced behavior shift, and why PDP enables stable behavior steering. Top: Standard evaluations vary observations while the intended behavior remains unchanged. Middle: We study constraint-induced behavior shifts, where environmental changes invalidate many of the trajectory modes in the training dataset, and success requires selecting or discovering a different trajectory mode. Bottom: In standard DP, steering via the sampling noise is ill-conditioned: small perturbations can lead to large, unpredictable trajectory changes. PDP, by contrast, exposes a learned behavior latent z whose geometry is aligned with trajectory similarity, so small changes in z induce smooth changes in behavior, enabling interpolation and adaptation.
abstract: We propose Parameterized Diffusion Policy (PDP), a framework for learning diffusion policies conditioned on low-dimensional, continuous parameters embedded in a learned behavior manifold. By constructing this manifold so that distances between latent representations reflect the semantic similarity between physical trajectories, we transform diffusion from a mechanism for stochastic diversity into a precise and optimizable tool for behavior steering. Our approach enables smooth interpolation between known strategies and efficient adaptation to novel constraints without updating policy weights. We demonstrate that PDP significantly improves adaptation performance on complex multimodal benchmarks in both simulated and real-robot experiments compared to standard diffusion policies, particularly in scenarios requiring the synthesis of novel behaviors.
